newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel embarrassing Bonn with gold plan-institutes.
newsitem.headline: Waigel embarrassing Bonn with gold plan-institutes.

text.p: Leading German economic institutes have accused Finance Minister Theo Waigel of embarrassing Germany and playing accounting tricks by seeking to revalue the Bundesbank's gold reserves to cut the public debt and deficit.

"It is unsolid. It is also embarrassing in front of other Europeans," Heiner Flassbeck, director of the Institut fuer Wirtschaftsforschung in Berlin, told Bild am Sonntag newspaper published on Sunday.
"Waigel always played the pope of correctness in front of them. Now we are finding he is preaching water while drinking wine."

Klaus-Werner Schatz, vice president of Kiel-based Institut fuer Weltwirtschaft, said, "We mocked Italy with its Eurotax, that is no longer possible," and that Waigel was engaging in the "tricks of a bookkeeper."
Italy introduced the Eurotax as part of a campaign to qualify for the planned single currency.

Under a controversial plan announced on Thursday, Waigel is seeking to revalue Bundesbank gold and currency reserves to plug holes in Germany's finances and improve its chances of qualifying for monetary union.

Those chances received a setback after an official estimate said 1997 tax revenue would be 18 billion marks less than previously forecast, casting further doubt on whether Germany can meet the Maastricht Treaty's fiscal convergence criteria.
The Treaty sets ceilings for a nation's public deficit and debt of three percent and 60 percent of gross domestic product, respectively, but allows overshoots in special circumstances.
"What he is planning can only be done once. Then the instrument is gone," said Udo Ludwig, director of the Halle-based Institut fuer Wirtschaftsordnung.
Flassbeck at Berlin-based IW said the Bundesbank's cautious gold and dollar valuation had contributed to Germany being regarded as world champion of solidity.
"Changing this in connection with the tax estimate leaves a very bad aftertaste."
